# FDG3057

> DO add the suffix “Dictionary.” Note that `IDictionary` is a specific type of collection, but this guideline takes precedence over the more general collections guideline that follows.

Framework Design Guidelines, 3rd edition, section 3.5.2 Names of Common Types. Applies to: IDictionary IDictionary&lt;TKey, TValue>.

## How it is checked

- Check: sdk (partial coverage)
- Diagnostics: CA1710
- Automatic fix: not applied automatically (the fix can break callers)
- Severity: library warning, application warning, test none
- Status: verified

CA1710 reports a type that implements IDictionary&lt;TKey, TValue> or IDictionary, also through a base class such as Dictionary&lt;TKey, TValue> because the package sets dotnet_code_quality.CA1710.exclude_indirect_base_types = false (see FDG3048; probe with SDK 10.0.403), when its name ends with neither Dictionary nor Collection. It also accepts Collection for a dictionary, although the book puts the Dictionary suffix first for such types, so coverage is partial. Renaming a public type changes the public API, so the fix is breaking; CA1710 has no code fix.
